exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Director, Cathay two five one, passing seven thousand feet descending to five thousand feet, heading two fow-er zero, Information Hotel.
exchanges.meaning: Approach check-in: descending 7,000 to 5,000 ft on heading 240, with ATIS Hotel received.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Director, radar contact, fly heading two fow-er zero, vector for ILS Runway zero sev-en left, number two in sequence.
exchanges.meaning: Radar contact established: continue heading 240 as a vector for ILS Runway 07L; the aircraft is number two in the arrival sequence.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Fly heading two fow-er zero, vector for ILS Runway zero sev-en left, number two, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Full readback of the vector heading, ILS approach intent and sequence position, with the callsign last.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, turn right heading zero fow-er zero, descend to three thousand feet, maintain wun eight zero knots.
exchanges.meaning: Tactical sequencing vector: right turn to heading 040, descend to 3,000 ft and hold 180 knots until established.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Turn right heading zero fow-er zero, descend to three thousand feet, speed wun eight zero knots, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Readback of the heading turn, descent and speed control, with the callsign last.

vocabulary.definition: ATC's stated tactical intent that the current heading is being issued to position the aircraft onto the ILS final approach course — a vector is NOT an approach clearance.
Terminal pattern leg flown parallel to but opposite the landing runway direction, where approach radar spaces and sequences arrivals.
Terminal pattern leg flown perpendicular to the runway after the downwind turn, leading to the intercept turn onto final.
Relative arrival-sequence position among terminal arrivals (e.g. "number two in sequence"), telling the crew its order to the runway.
The closing turn (max 30° per ICAO Doc 4444) from the intercept heading onto the localizer course.
Speed-control restriction for sequencing that stays in effect until the aircraft is established on the final approach course.
Approach radar control position providing tactical vectors and sequencing in the terminal area around the airport.
Extra in-trail distance behind heavy-category aircraft (including the Boeing 757, treated as a heavy) whose vortices can roll over lighter followers.
Standard Terminal Arrival Route — the published instrument procedure flown before handoff to Director for radar vectors.
The ILS vertical guidance path; the pilot must not descend on it until explicitly cleared for the approach.

quiz.question: When an air traffic controller vectors an aircraft to intercept an instrument final approach course, what is the maximum recommended intercept angle under ICAO Doc 4444?
quiz.explanation: Under standard ICAO radar vectoring criteria, the closing turn onto the localizer or final approach track should not exceed 30 degrees (up to 45° in specific airspace configurations) to ensure smooth capture without overshooting.

quiz.question: What is the primary operational distinction between "Vector for ILS approach" and "Cleared ILS approach"?
options: "Vector for ILS" is a heading instruction toward the localizer; "Cleared ILS" authorizes the pilot to track the localizer and descend on the glide path.
"Vector for ILS" authorizes landing on the runway.
quiz.explanation: A vector is strictly a tactical heading assignment. Only when the clearance "Cleared ILS approach" is explicitly issued is the pilot authorized to intercept and track the localizer and descend on the glideslope.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body:
| Phrase / Command | ICAO Standard Definition | Phonetic Guide | Operational Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vector for ILS Runway [num] | Stating tactical intent of approach radar vectoring. | VEK-tor for eye-el-ess... | "Fly heading 240, vector for ILS Runway 07L." |
| Downwind / Base leg | Standard legs of the terminal radar rectangular pattern. | DOWN-wind / BASE leg | Positions aircraft parallel/perpendicular to runway. |
| Number [num] in sequence | Relative arrival sequence position among terminal arrivals. | NUM-ber [DI-GIT] in SEE-kwens | "Number two in sequence behind B777." |
| Turn to intercept [course] | Closing turn onto the localizer (max 30° intercept angle). | turn to in-ter-SEPT... | "Turn right heading 040 to intercept." |
| Maintain [speed] until established | Speed control applied for sequencing onto final approach. | mayn-TAYN [speed] un-TIL es-TAB-lisht | "Maintain 180 knots until established." |

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body:
- **Day 28 Review (+1d):** Descending through Transition Level, reset subscale from Standard 1013.25 hPa back to airport QNH.
- **Day 14 Review (+14d):** On radar vectors, steer assigned compass heading without applying wind crab.

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact — Why the B757 is Treated as a Heavy
sections.body: Although the Boeing 757's maximum takeoff weight (115 tonnes) places it in the ICAO "Medium" weight class, its exceptionally high-lift supercritical wing produces wake vortices as violent as those generated by a Boeing 747! Following several fatal rollover crashes involving smaller aircraft trailing 757s in the 1990s, aviation authorities created a dedicated wake turbulence category for the 757, requiring full 4-to-5-mile heavy spacing behind it!
